# zone_domain_contact (Resource)

A registry contact attached to a domain.

Registries normalise contact details and some reject changes outright, so most arguments here are optional and computed: whatever is not configured takes the value the registry holds.

~> **The registrant contact usually cannot be replaced this way.** Registries treat a change of registrant as a trade, with its own process and often a fee. Expect the API to refuse a destroy or a role change on a registrant.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A technical contact. Registries normalise contact details, so anything left
# unset takes the value the registry already holds.
resource "zone_domain_contact" "tech" {
  domain = "example.com"
  role   = "tech"

  name    = "Example Operations"
  email   = "noc@example.com"
  voice   = "+372.5551234"
  country = "EE"
}

# An .ee registrant needs an identity code, which is what the ext_ident fields
# are for. Which of them a registry wants depends on the TLD.
resource "zone_domain_contact" "registrant" {
  domain = "example.com"
  role   = "registrant"

  name         = "Example OU"
  organization = "Example OU"
  email        = "owner@example.com"
  voice        = "+372.5551234"
  country      = "EE"
  city         = "Tallinn"
  street       = "Narva mnt 1"
  postalcode   = "10117"

  ext_ident      = "12345678"
  ext_ident_type = "company_number"
  ext_ident_cc   = "EE"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain` (String) Domain this contact belongs to, for example `example.com`.
- `role` (String) What this contact is for: `registrant`, `admin` or `tech`. Changing it forces a new contact.

### Optional

- `city` (String) City.
- `country` (String) Two-letter ISO country code, for example `EE`.
- `email` (String) Contact email address.
- `ext_country_of_citizenship` (String) Registry extension, meaningful only for some TLDs. Country of citizenship.
- `ext_department` (String) Registry extension, meaningful only for some TLDs. Department within the organisation.
- `ext_ident` (String) Registry extension, meaningful only for some TLDs. Identity or registration number. Required for an `.ee` registrant, together with `ext_ident_type` and `ext_ident_cc`.
- `ext_ident_cc` (String) Registry extension, meaningful only for some TLDs. Country that issued `ext_ident`, as a two-letter code.
- `ext_ident_type` (String) Registry extension, meaningful only for some TLDs. What `ext_ident` holds: `private_number`, `company_number` or `birthday`.
- `ext_language` (String) Registry extension, meaningful only for some TLDs. Preferred language.
- `ext_legal_form` (String) Registry extension, meaningful only for some TLDs. Legal form of the organisation.
- `ext_passport` (String) Registry extension, meaningful only for some TLDs. Passport number.
- `ext_vatnr` (String) Registry extension, meaningful only for some TLDs. VAT number.
- `fax` (String) Fax number, if the registry still asks for one.
- `first_name` (String) Given name.
- `last_name` (String) Family name.
- `name` (String) Full name. Set this or `first_name` and `last_name`.
- `organization` (String) Organisation, when the contact is a company.
- `postalcode` (String) Postal code.
- `state` (String) State or county, where the registry uses one.
- `street` (String) Street address.
- `voice` (String) Telephone number in international form, for example `+372.5551234`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Identifier assigned by zone.eu. Documented as a number and returned as a string, so it is a string here and both forms are accepted.
- `registry_handle` (String) The registry's own identifier for this contact. Read-only.
- `resource_url` (String) API URL of this contact.
- `type` (String) Contact type as zone.eu classifies it. Read-only.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Contacts are imported as "<domain>/<contact id>". The id is visible in the
# resource_url of an existing contact, or from the API.
terraform import zone_domain_contact.tech "example.com/12345"
```
